housing.title: Housing & Real Estate
housing.overview: Whether you're renting for your first year or purchasing your forever home, understanding Spain's housing market can help you make informed decisions before you relocate.

blocks.text: Renting can offer flexibility while you adjust to your new life, especially if you're unfamiliar with the area you're moving to. Buying may make sense if you're planning to stay long term, have established residency plans, or are investing in property.

transportation.title: Transportation & Driving
transportation.overview: Spain has one of Europe's most efficient transportation systems, and many expats are pleasantly surprised to discover they may not need a car at all. Whether a car makes sense for you will largely depend on where you choose to live.

subsections.title: Do You Need a Car in Spain?

residency.title: Residency Documents
residency.overview: Several important documents will become part of your daily life in Spain. Understanding them ahead of time can make your transition significantly smoother.

blocks.text: The NIE, or Número de Identidad de Extranjero, is your Foreigner Identification Number. Think of it as your official identification number for many administrative activities in Spain.
For many expats, obtaining an NIE is one of the first administrative steps after deciding to move.

The TIE, or Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero, is your physical residency card. Unlike the NIE, which is simply a number, the TIE serves as proof of your legal residency status in Spain. The card generally includes:
Many non-EU residents will eventually need a TIE as part of their immigration process.
Your NIE and TIE are used throughout nearly every aspect of life in Spain. You'll often need them when:
Because these documents are so important, it's beneficial to understand the application process before arriving.
